title: Offset pagination skips eligible profiles after each bulk update
reasoning: The command stores an initial count, then processes a mutable queryset using offset slices. In the default path, each successful bulk_update changes timezone away from UTC/empty, so those rows no longer match the queryset filter. The next slice is then applied to the smaller remaining result set, skipping the next batch of still-eligible profiles. For example, with 250 matching profiles and batch size 100, after saving the first 100, slice [100:200] is evaluated against the 150 remaining matches and skips the original profiles 101-200.
recommendation: Materialize stable primary keys before updating, or iterate with keyset pagination over IDs and fetch each batch by that fixed ID list. Avoid offset slicing on a queryset whose membership is changed by the command.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this command, and the bug requires more than one batch of eligible profiles to expose the skipped middle batch.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create more than 100 profiles matching the default UTC/empty timezone filter, mock TimezoneFinder to return a timezone for all of them, run the command, and assert every initially eligible profile was updated.
minimumFixScope: Change update_user_timezones.py batching to use a stable list/query of profile IDs before mutating timezone values.
